## Summary

Eisman attributes market swings to changing war and credit narratives, flags retail and institutional redemption pressure, and remains cautious on solar and health insurance. The Elevance regulatory problem was real, but the threatened sanctions were conditional and later recorded as corrected. He explicitly leaves AI-driven mass unemployment and life-insurer credit losses unproven. His categorical no-credit-cycle-since-GFC statement is too broad; evidence of market anxiety is distinct from realized systemic loss.

Full transcript read. This bounded evidence audit retains unresolved outcomes where matched primary verification is missing; those are not adverse accuracy grades.

### 016. CMS threatened to stop Elevance Medicare Advantage enrollment and restrict communications from March 31 because of risk-adjustment submission failures.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 10:29-11:18](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LfL3Bh3rics&t=629s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The CMS notice confirms the threatened enrollment and communication sanctions, with an explicit corrective-action route.

Qualification: This was conditional on failure to correct, not a permanent ban.

Assessment test: Establish whether the stated elevance sanctions proposition holds using matched primary disclosures; retain its conditions and separate causal explanations from price movements.

- [Elevance notice of intermediate sanctions](https://www.cms.gov/files/document/elevancehealthsanction02272026.pdf) (2026-02-27): CMS identified rejected encrypted USB submissions and failure to correct unsupported diagnoses. March 31 sanctions were conditional on failure to complete corrective steps by March 30, not an unavoidable permanent enrollment prohibition.

### 024. There has been no credit cycle since the GFC.

**Wrong** | Steve Eisman | explanation | supporting

[Source at 14:49-15:07](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LfL3Bh3rics&t=889s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The literal claim conflicts with multiple post-GFC increases in loan charge-offs; absence of another systemic GFC is narrower.

Assessment test: Establish whether the stated no credit cycle proposition holds using matched primary disclosures; retain its conditions and separate causal explanations from price movements.

- [Large bank consumer credit card net charge-off rate](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/data/RCCCBNCOPCT) (2026-10-07): Quarterly series rises from 2.99% in 2015Q3 to 5.03% in 2020Q2, and from 1.93% in 2021Q4 to 6.01% in 2025Q1. This contradicts literally no post-GFC episode of increasing loan losses, without establishing a systemic crisis.

## Framework and tools

- Distinguish a narrative reversal from new realized losses.
- Look for loan growth and weak diligence before credit trouble.
- Follow financing costs and subsidies in solar.
- Separate duration matching at insurers from asset credit and hidden leverage concerns.
